relevance_reason: Reports new patients with COQ7-related primary CoQ10 deficiency, including a late-onset form with progressive neuropathy and lower extremity weakness (the HMNR9 phenotype), plus yeast functional studies of COQ7 variants such as the p.[Thr103Met;Leu111Pro] complex allele.

findings.statement: Wongkittichote et al. (2023) reported 5 new patients with COQ7-related primary CoQ10 deficiency. They described two distinct presentations: a neonatal-onset form with severe neuromuscular, cardiorespiratory, and renal involvement, and a late-onset form with progressive neuropathy, lower extremity weakness, abnormal gait, and variable developmental delay.
quotes: We identified five new patients with COQ7-related primary CoQ10 deficiency

The main clinical features included a neonatal-onset presentation with severe neuromuscular, cardiorespiratory and renal involvement and a late-onset disease presenting with progressive neuropathy, lower extremity weakness, abnormal gait, and variable developmental delay.

findings.statement: Wongkittichote et al. (2023) studied previously reported and newly found COQ7 variants in a yeast cat5-deletion model (CAT5 is the yeast ortholog of COQ7). Wildtype CAT5 completely rescued the oxidative growth defect, but yeast CAT5 carrying the equivalent human pathogenic variants did not. Variants equivalent to human p.Arg54Gln, p.Arg107Trp, p.Ile66Asn, and the complex allele p.[Thr103Met;Leu111Pro] partially rescued growth, which the authors took to mean that these are hypomorphic alleles.
quotes: Expression of wild-type CAT5 could completely rescue the defect; however, yeast CAT5 harboring equivalent human pathogenic variants could not.

cat5Δ yeast harboring p.Arg57Gln (equivalent to human p.Arg54Gln), p.Arg112Trp (equivalent to p.Arg107Trp), p.Ile69Asn (equivalent to p.Ile66Asn) and combination of p.Lys108Met and p.Leu116Pro (equivalent to the complex allele p.[Thr103Met;Leu111Pro]) partially rescued the growth defects, indicating these variants are hypomorphic alleles.

findings.statement: Wongkittichote et al. (2023) defined two distinct presentations of COQ7-related disorder, a severe neonatal-onset form and a late-onset neuropathy form, and reported an emerging genotype-phenotype correlation in which several variants behaved as hypomorphic (leaky) alleles in yeast.
quotes: Overall, we define two distinct disease presentations of COQ7-related disorder with emerging genotype-phenotype correlation and validate the use of the yeast model for functional studies of COQ7 variants.

findings.statement: Wongkittichote et al. (2023) found that 2,4-dihydroxybenzoic acid (2,4-diHB) supplementation rescued the oxidative growth defect of cat5-deleted yeast carrying either leaky or severe mutants. COQ8 overexpression combined with 2,4-diHB acted synergistically to restore oxidative growth and the respiratory defect.
quotes: Supplementation with 2,4 dihydroxybenzoic acid (2,4-diHB) rescued the growth defect of both the leaky and severe mutants.
Overexpression of COQ8 and 2,4-diHB supplementation synergistically restored oxidative growth and respiratory defect.

relevance_reason: Reports a consanguineous Syrian family with distal hereditary motor neuropathy caused by a homozygous COQ7 start-loss variant, with functional studies; directly defines HMNR9.

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2023) reported 3 sibs (a 24-year-old woman and men aged 23 and 12 years), born to Syrian first-cousin parents, with a progressive, severe length-dependent motor neuropathy. Distal weakness developed by 10 to 14 years of age, with muscle atrophy in the distal lower more than upper limbs, preserved sensation in all modalities, and preserved deep tendon reflexes. The patients had no developmental delay, cognitive impairment, or upper motor neuron features. Gene panels for Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, SMA, distal HMN, and mtDNA were negative.
quotes: We report 3 affected siblings (sibling 1: female aged 24 years, sibling 2: male aged 23 years, and sibling 3: male aged 12 years) referred for progressive distal weakness to the Medical Genetics service for evaluation. The siblings were born to Syrian parents who are first cousins.

The 3 affected siblings developed distal weakness by 10–14 years of age and muscle atrophy in the distal lower more than upper extremities with preserved sensation (temperature, fine touch, sharp, vibration, and proprioception) and preserved deep tendon reflexes.
The siblings had no developmental delay or cognitive impairment and no upper motor neuron features.

phenotypes.text: distal muscle atrophy, lower more than upper limbs

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2023) found that electrodiagnostic testing in all 3 affected sibs showed reduced distal motor amplitudes with preserved sensory responses, and needle EMG showed distal chronic reinnervation without active denervation; there was no evidence of demyelination.
quotes: Electrodiagnostic testing of all affected siblings revealed reduced distal motor amplitude pattern with preserved sensory responses. Needle EMG studies demonstrated distal chronic reinnervation with no active denervation.
a pure motor length–dependent neuropathy with no clinical or electrophysiologic evidence of sensory nerve involvement and no evidence of demyelination

phenotypes.text: reduced distal compound motor action potential amplitudes
phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased compound muscle action potential amplitude

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2023) reported that muscle MRI in 2 sibs showed normal proximal muscles with distal muscle wasting and moderate to severe fat infiltration beginning at the distal third of the thigh and most pronounced in the calves, particularly soleus and gastrocnemius. Vastus lateralis biopsy in 1 sib showed neurogenic atrophy with angular atrophic fibers, pyknotic nuclear clumps, group atrophy, and fiber type grouping, without ragged red or cytochrome oxidase-negative fibers.
quotes: muscle MRI of siblings 1 and 2 demonstrated normal proximal musculature with significant distal muscle wasting and moderate to severe fat infiltration starting the level of the distal third of the thigh and most pronounced in the calves bilaterally

Muscle biopsy of left vastus lateralis of sibling 2 demonstrated neurogenic atrophy with wide variation in fiber size and shape due to the presence of scattered angular, atrophic fibers, occasionally in groups, as well as abundant pyknotic nuclear clumps.
There were no ragged red fibers or cytochrome oxidase negative fibers. Myofibrillar ATPase staining revealed group atrophy and fiber type grouping

phenotypes.text: fatty infiltration of distal leg muscles

findings.statement: In 3 sibs with distal hereditary motor neuropathy from a consanguineous Syrian family, Smith et al. (2023) identified a homozygous c.1A-G variant in the COQ7 gene (NM_016138.5), predicted to abolish the initiating methionine, by duo-exome sequencing with Sanger confirmation. The parents and an unaffected sib were heterozygous carriers, and the variant was absent from gnomAD. Translation was predicted to start at met39, removing the cleavable N-terminal mitochondrial targeting sequence and 2 additional amino acids.
quotes: duo-exome sequencing was performed on sibling 1 and sibling 2 and identified a shared homozygous variant of uncertain significance in COQ7 (NM_01638.5) c.1A > G p (Figure 1C). Affected sibling 3 also shared the homozygous, variant of uncertain significance in COQ7.
The parents and sibling 4 were heterozygous carriers for the COQ7 variant. The COQ7 variant was absent in gnomAD, and in silico prediction modeling predicted pathogenicity.

Exome sequencing demonstrated the homozygous COQ7 c.1A > G p.? variant that is expected to bypass the first 38 amino acid residues at the n-terminus, initiating instead with methionine at position 39.

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2023) found that fibroblasts from the 3 affected sibs had on average 87% lower CoQ10 than those of the carrier father and unaffected sib and accumulated the COQ7 substrate DMQ10, which was undetectable in carriers. Muscle from 1 sib had 67% lower CoQ10 than a control (63 vs 192.7 ng/mg protein) without detectable DMQ10. COQ7 protein was reduced by about 85% in patient fibroblasts and undetectable in muscle, whereas PDSS2 levels were unchanged.
quotes: On average, cultured fibroblasts from siblings 1, 2, and 3 had 87% lower CoQ10 than their father and unaffected sibling

Muscle CoQ10 in sibling 2 was 67% lower than muscle CoQ10 of the unrelated human donor (63 ng/mg protein vs 192.7 ng/mg protein) (Figure 4, A–C). However, no DMQ10 peak was seen in the muscle of sibling 2
The affected siblings had severely diminished levels of COQ7 in fibroblasts (Figure 3D), with COQ7 to porin ratios 85% ± 7% lower in affected siblings than their carrier father and sibling 4.

phenotypes.text: decreased coenzyme Q10 in fibroblasts and muscle
phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased level of coenzyme Q10 in skeletal muscle

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2023) found that permeabilized muscle from 1 affected sib had lower FCCP-induced maximal respiration and complex IV activity, higher H2O2 emission, and decreased complex I- and IV-containing supercomplexes than controls, with near-normal complex I and I+II respiration. Patient fibroblasts had reduced maximal and spare respiratory capacity, increased basal extracellular acidification, a glycolysis-favoring bioenergetic profile, and impaired metabolic flexibility, but remained viable in galactose medium.
quotes: FCCP-induced maximal mitochondrial respiration and CIV activity were lower in vastus lateralis muscle from sibling 2 compared with those in muscle from unrelated controls (Figure 5A). Simultaneous fluorometric analysis demonstrated higher H2O2 emissions in muscle from sibling 2
BN-PAGE analysis of skeletal muscle mitochondrial SC content demonstrated decreased content of complexes I and IV containing SCs in sibling 2
fibroblasts from affected siblings displayed impaired capacity to switch between ATP production pathways

phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial respiratory chain

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2023) reported congenital deafness in 2 of the affected sibs and in the unaffected sib, which did not segregate with the motor neuropathy. It was explained by a homozygous GJB2 c.35delG (p.Gly12ValfsTer2) variant, for which both parents were heterozygous carriers.
quotes: The deafness did not segregate with motor neuropathy (sibling 1 was not deaf and sibling 4 had no neuropathy)
for the 3 siblings who had congenital deafness (siblings 2, 3, and 4), genetic testing also revealed a homozygous GJB2 variant: c.35delG; p.(Gly12Valfs*2) (NM_004004.5)

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2023) postulated that the metabolic dysfunction and increased oxidative stress (elevated H2O2 emission) associated with CoQ10 deficiency contribute to the selective distal motor phenotype. They suggested that the increased H2O2 emission may be due to loss of nuclear-located COQ7.
quotes: Thus, the metabolic dysfunction observed in the fibroblasts and biopsied muscle of the affected patients combined with the elevated H2O2 emission observed in the biopsy with the observed neuropathy likely contribute to the distal motor phenotype.
the increased H2O2 emission observed in the permeabilized skeletal muscle of sibling 2 may be attributable to the lack of nuclear-located COQ7

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2023) stated that their family represented a distinct phenotype from previously reported COQ7-related primary CoQ10 deficiency. Earlier cases had demyelinating and axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy, developmental delay, and upper motor neuron features, and the authors described their family as the first report of pure distal hereditary motor neuropathy caused by COQ7.
quotes: Pure motor neuropathies are rare, and the clinical presentation of the family reported in this study represents a distinct phenotype from previously reported cases of COQ7-related CoQ10 deficiency.
we present the first report of pure distal hereditary motor neuropathy associated with a homozygous pathogenic variant in the gene encoding the ubiquinone biosynthesis protein COQ7

relevance_reason: Title reports biallelic COQ7 variants causing distal hereditary motor neuropathy in two Chinese families, which directly defines this entry.

findings.statement: Liu et al. (2023) reported biallelic variants in the COQ7 gene causing distal hereditary motor neuropathy in 2 Chinese families.
quotes: Biallelic variants in the COQ7 gene cause distal hereditary motor neuropathy in two Chinese families.

relevance_reason: First report of a family with distal hereditary motor neuropathy caused by homozygous COQ7 start-codon variant, with clinical, molecular and functional data.

findings.statement: Jacquier et al. (2023) reported 3 Portuguese sibs (2 brothers and a sister, aged 36, 25, and 42 years) born to nonconsanguineous healthy parents with an axonal, recessively inherited distal hereditary motor neuropathy. Onset was between ages 9 and 12 years with walking difficulties, followed by progressive distal weakness predominantly in the lower limbs, later hand involvement, amyotrophy, and pes cavus in all; sensory examination was normal and there was no cognitive disorder. Two had pyramidal signs (brisk reflexes and Hoffman sign in one, left Babinski sign in another), and achilles reflexes were abolished in 2; 2 were ambulant without help and the eldest used ankle-foot orthoses.
quotes: The affected siblings were born from non-consanguineous healthy parents in Portugal (Table 1). The family displayed an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern.
All of the patients presented with length-dependent pure motor axonal neuropathy, leading to progressive walking difficulties and disability, with childhood onset.
Deep tendon reflexes were brisk in the four limbs (except for Achilles reflexes which were abolished), and a Hoffman’s sign was found, without Babinski’s sign or spasticity.

phenotypes.text: amyotrophy of lower limbs and hands

findings.statement: Jacquier et al. (2023) found on electrophysiologic studies in 2 patients evidence of a pure motor axonal neuropathy predominantly affecting the distal lower limbs, with fibrillations and neurogenic recruitment. In the index patient, brain and spinal cord MRI, echocardiography, ECG, and audiometry were normal, and creatine kinase was mildly elevated (215 U/l).
quotes: There was evidence of a pure motor axonal neuropathy predominantly affecting the distal part of the lower limbs.
Brain and spinal cord MRI were normal. Transthoracic echocardiography and ECG were normal.
Biological testing showed a mild elevation of the creatine phosphokinase (CPK) level (215 U/l, normal <200 U/l).

findings.statement: In 3 sibs with distal hereditary motor neuropathy, Jacquier et al. (2023) identified by whole-exome sequencing a homozygous c.3G>T variant in the start codon of COQ7 isoform 1 (NM_016138.5; p.Met1?). The variant segregated with disease (parents heterozygous), was absent from ExAC, and was present once in heterozygous state in gnomAD (allele frequency 0.000004065). Alternative isoforms 2 and 3 use other start codons and were predicted unaffected.
quotes: only one variant, which was absent from the ExAC database but present once at the heterogenous state in gnomAD database (allele frequency 0.000004065) was shared by the three patients in a homozygous state and present in their unaffected parents in a heterozygous state, confirming the segregation
The variant was a G>T substitution in the start codon of the longest transcript (isoform 1, NM_016138.5, c.3G>T; NP_057222.2, p.Met1?)

findings.statement: Jacquier et al. (2023) showed that the c.3G>T COQ7 mutation reduced COQ7 protein by 85% in transfected SH-EP neuroblastoma cells without changing mRNA levels or subcellular localization, and that COQ7 protein was barely detectable in patient fibroblasts while mRNA was only modestly decreased (17-21%), suggesting a translation initiation defect. A FLAG-tagged isoform 2 localized to mitochondria, suggesting other isoforms could partially compensate.
quotes: COQ7 levels were reduced by 85% in SH-EP cells expressing the mutant COQ7 compared to SH-EP cells expressing the wild-type COQ7
COQ7 protein was barely detected in the patient’s fibroblasts, whereas it was easily detected in control cells (Fig. 3B), suggesting a drastic reduction in the COQ7 protein level.

these results suggest that the translation of COQ7 isoform 1 is impacted by the variant and that other isoforms of the protein can provide mitochondria with COQ7, suggesting that they could partially compensate for the loss of isoform 1.

findings.statement: Jacquier et al. (2023) found decreased CoQ10 in fibroblasts from the index patient (12.5 vs 71.5 pmol/mg protein in controls) with accumulation of 6-demethoxycoenzyme Q10 (6-DMQ), the COQ7 substrate; 6-DMQ was also detected in the patient's plasma. The authors suggested that plasma 6-DMQ accumulation could be used to confirm pathogenicity of COQ7 variants.
quotes: We observed a major decrease in the CoQ10 level from 71.5 pmol/mg of protein in control fibroblasts to 12.5 pmol/mg of protein in patient fibroblasts together with the appearance of 6-DMQ in the fibroblasts of the patient compared with the controls
The appearance of 6-DMQ was also found in the patient’s plasma (Fig. 4B).
When COQ7 variants are identified, the accumulation of 6-DMQ levels in the plasma observed herein will be useful to confirm the pathogenicity of these variants.

findings.statement: Jacquier et al. (2023) showed that patient fibroblasts had reduced mitochondrial ATP production (42% vs 56-63% in controls) with increased glycolytic ATP production, reduced basal and maximal respiration, and reduced proliferation in galactose medium. Treatment with 2,4-dihydroxybenzoic acid normalized 6-DMQ and slightly increased CoQ10, and CoQ10 supplementation rescued respiration and proliferation. They speculated that milder disease than with previously reported catalytic-domain COQ7 mutations reflects sparing of alternative isoforms.
quotes: A Seahorse analysis (ATP rate assay) showed that mitochondrial ATP production was decreased from 63.3% or 56.4% in control fibroblasts to 42% in the patient’s fibroblasts (Fig. 4F)
This reduced mitochondrial ATP production is explained by a decrease in the activity of the respiratory chain, which can be rescued by CoQ10 supplementation.

We speculate that in our patient the mutation affects only the translation of the main COQ7 isoform, and does not affect the two other COQ7 isoforms, and as a consequence does not completely prevent CoQ10 synthesis.

findings.statement: Jacquier et al. (2023) reported that the affected sister had symptom stabilization between ages 15 and 18 years while taking CoQ10 (30 mg/day), with renewed progression after stopping supplementation at 18 years. The authors suggested oral CoQ10 supplementation as a potential therapy.
quotes: Between 15 and 18 years of age, while she was treated with CoQ10 (30 mg per day), she reported symptom stabilization. A new progressive worsening started at the age of 18 years and the stop of CoQ10 supplementation.
